All cases sequester the CO offsite. 2 2 COST AND PERFORMANCE BASELINE FOR FOSSIL ENERGY PLANTS VOLUME 1: BITUMINOUS COAL AND NATURAL GAS TO ELECTRICITY All plant configurations were evaluated based on installation at a greenfield site. Capacity factors (CFs) utilized were 80 percent for all IGCC configurations, and 85 percent for all PC and NGCC configurations. Availability is defined as the percent of time during a specific period that a generating unit is capable of producing electricity. This report assumes that each new plant would be dispatched any time it is available and would be capable of generating the nameplate capacity when online. Therefore, CF and availability are equal. The calculations assume that the CF and availability are constant over the life of the plant. These plants are considered to be built for a thirty-year life, are well-maintained plants with sufficient and adequate maintenance budgets, and are operated in a manner that supports the assumed CF.
